name: Opening Break
plain_words: The one signal that survived the 1,492: a break away from the session open by 0.45 of the 14-day range, confirmed by a 5-minute close on the right side of the day's VWAP, taken once per day before 11:00 ET, stop 0.25 of the range, target 0.60, flat by 15:50. Re-run on Nasdaq and S&P futures at micro-contract cost.
caught: SANDBOX_PROMPT_v2 described the proven signal as a 'first-30-minute range break'. The proven rule (CHALLENGE_BACKTEST_V2 / LIMIT_FILL_REPORT) is the volatility-band break above; the 30-minute-range form is declared separately below as its first fix candidate so the two are never confused.

cost.note: $1.22 per round turn per micro contract + 1 tick slippage per side (2 ticks round trip)

firm.name: futures prop account (Topstep-style 50K)
firm.note: daily loss = self-imposed $1,000; max loss = $2,000 trailing end-of-day; flat before 16:10 ET

pass_line.note: tightened 2026-09-14 before any verdict was adopted: 'sized so the firm's rules hold' is evaluated as the LARGEST risk per trade at which they hold, and the strategy must earn >= 10%/yr of the account at that size — an edge that only survives at a size that earns nothing is not a pass

expectation: OOS 0.00 to +0.05R net at 1 tick per side. The lab's own SPX table put OOS at +0.018R (0.25 tick) and -0.032R (0.5 tick); NQ's wider point range may carry it. Honest odds of a pass: about 1 in 3.

fixes.name: Opening Break — range form
fixes.why: a wider stop (the other side of the first 30-minute range) makes each tick of cost a smaller fraction of R
